items.stemHtml: A 61-year-old man has 1 year of episodic facial flushing and watery diarrhea. Over the past 2 months he has developed a rough, scaly, darkly pigmented rash on the backs of his hands, forearms and the front of his neck, and his family notes forgetfulness. CT shows multiple liver masses and a small ileal mass. Urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid excretion is markedly raised. A deficiency of which of the following best explains the skin and mental changes?

options.label: A
options.html: Cobalamin, from ileal involvement by the tumour

options.label: B
options.html: Niacin, from diversion of tryptophan to serotonin

options.label: C
options.html: Pyridoxine, from increased use in serotonin synthesis

options.label: D
options.html: Riboflavin, from malabsorption in chronic diarrhea

options.label: E
options.html: Thiamine, from tumour consumption of glucose

items.explanationHtml:
Metastatic carcinoid tumour makes large amounts of serotonin from tryptophan. Normally a small fraction of dietary tryptophan is used to make niacin (as NAD); when the tumour diverts tryptophan to serotonin, niacin deficiency (pellagra) follows: photosensitive dermatitis, diarrhea and dementia. The raised 5-HIAA confirms the serotonin output; nicotinamide supplementation treats the pellagra.

Takeaway: carcinoid syndrome can cause pellagra because tumour serotonin synthesis consumes tryptophan, a niacin precursor.

whyNot.A: B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and posterior column disease, not a photosensitive pigmented dermatitis.
whyNot.C: Pyridoxine is a cofactor for decarboxylases, but deficiency gives cheilosis, neuropathy and sideroblastic anemia, and carcinoid does not classically deplete it.
whyNot.D: Riboflavin deficiency causes angular cheilitis, glossitis and corneal changes, not sun-exposed scaly pigmentation with dementia.
whyNot.E: Thiamine deficiency causes beriberi or Wernicke encephalopathy, not dermatitis.

items.objective: Explain pellagra in carcinoid syndrome through diversion of tryptophan to serotonin.
